name: device writes its own status
why: The normal 15 s telemetry write from the firmware, authenticated with the device's own token.

name: device writes another device's status
why: A stolen or cloned device token must not be able to impersonate a different incubator.

name: device updates one field of its status
why: A single-child write; the parent's hasChildren .validate sees the merged data, so it passes because the status already exists.

name: device writes a partial status to a fresh node
why: On a device with no status yet, a write missing 'hum' and 'heater' fails the hasChildren rule.

name: device writes an out-of-range temperature
why: A broken SHT31 reports -45 or 130; the rule keeps garbage out of the database.

name: device writes a status with an unknown field
why: Schema drift: the $other rule rejects fields the apps do not know about.

name: device writes a status with a far-future timestamp
why: ts must be at most 5 minutes ahead of the server clock; 4102444800 is the year 2100.

name: device writes a status with a string temperature
why: Type check: '26.9' is a string, not a number.

name: device appends a history entry
why: History keys are 10-digit epoch seconds and the entry must not exist yet.

name: device overwrites an existing history entry
why: History is append-only: a compromised device cannot rewrite the record.

name: device deletes a history entry
why: Writing null is a delete; the .write rule requires newData.exists().

name: device appends history under a malformed key
why: A push() key or a millisecond timestamp is refused, so the history stays sortable by second.

name: device reads its own control node
why: The firmware polls /control for the target temperature; the device may read its own subtree.

name: device writes its own control node
why: Only an owner may set the target temperature; a device must not be able to raise its own setpoint.

name: device reads another device
why: One device's token gives no visibility into other incubators.

name: token without the device claim writes status
why: A plain user token that happens to carry a deviceId claim is still not a device.
